sections.skill: Design fair methods for awkward numbers

branch.new_demand: Build fair methods when the number of people does not divide the outcomes.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions
questions.skill: Design fair methods for awkward numbers
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Five people must be chosen from fairly with one fair die. Which method works?
questions.prompt_markup: Five people must be chosen from fairly with one fair die. Which method works?

choices.text: Assign 1-5 to the people and give 6 to the first person.
Assign 1-5 to the people; on a 6, roll again.
Assign 1-6 and let the sixth face mean "everyone".
Roll and divide the result by 5.

questions.correct_answer: Assign 1-5 to the people; on a 6, roll again.
questions.grading_note: Rolling again until a 1-5 comes up keeps 1/5 each; the others favor one person or do not pick exactly one person.

questions.target_skill: Design fair methods for awkward numbers
